ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (as consolidated) regulating Private Interest Foundations; Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT) as amended by Ley 70 de 30 de enero de 2019 creating the Beneficial Owner Registry and reinforcing UBO disclosure obligations; Decreto Ejecutivo No. 166 de 21 de agosto de 2015 (AML regulatory implementing rules).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Private Interest Foundation Charter and Statutory Supplement (Acto Constitutivo y Reglamento de la Fundación de Interés Privado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian Notary Public or foreign Notary Public with legalized signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for members of the Apostille Convention; otherwise Panamanian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Acceptance of Appointment of Resident Agent (Aceptación del Agente Residente) with Registered Office Address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian licensed attorney and registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Panamanian notarization; domestic issuance, no apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copies of Ultimate Beneficial Owner Identification and Proof of Address (Passport and Utility Bill or Bank Reference)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Civil registry/notary of origin country or qualified certifying officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Panamanian Consular Legalization for each UBO document

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory politically exposed person (PEP) screening, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU/UK sanctions, and Panama's Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) risk-alert screening for all founders, council members, beneficiaries, signatories, and financial intermediaries. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for high-risk jurisdictions, politically exposed persons, or any transaction routed through trust, shell, or secrecy-prone structures. Screening must be refreshed at least every six months and before each qualifying financial transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Portal de Servicios Digitales del Registro Público de Panamá - Reserva de Nombres en Línea (Registro Publico de Panama Online Name Reservation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names may be submitted in Spanish or English, or in any language using Latin script; all non-Spanish names must include a Spanish translation or Latin-character transliteration for public registry indexing. The foundation name must end with 'Foundation' or 'Fundación' and must not be verbatim identical or phonetically confusingly similar to an existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a 'Recurso de Reconsideración' with the Director General of the Registro Público de Panamá within five (5) working days of the rejection notification. The appeal must include a revised name proposal or legal arguments showing alignment with Law 25 of 1995 and registry naming regulations. Unresolved appeals may be escalated as a hierarchical remedy before the 'Viceministerio de Registro Público' and ultimately through judicial review before the Contencioso Administrativo jurisdiction.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible at the upstream corporate level for mail forwarding and service-of-process purposes through the registered agent, provided the registered agent maintains the statutory physical address in Panama. However, for the DTC brand e-commerce business, payment processors and regulated PSPs (Shopify Payments, PayPal, Stripe) generally require demonstrable commercial substance: active business management, sales records, fulfillment or warehouse contracts, and a business bank account. A pure virtual office without underlying commercial evidence will not satisfy standard know-your-customer and underwriting review.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate likelihood quantified at approximately 3-8% per annum under risk-based AML/CFT supervision by the Panamanian UAF, banking AML officers, and registered-agent compliance oversight; the probability increases if the foundation holds significant payment float, processes high card-acquiring volumes, or maintains accounts with regulated Panamanian banks subject to on-site verification protocols.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended by Law No. 20 of 2017; particularly Articles 18–25 (charter content, endowment, registered office, Resident Agent) and Article 68; complemented by Law 70 of 2019 (beneficial ownership and AML duties of Resident Agents) and Executive Decree 24 of 2019.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) — Private Interest Foundations Section, Mercantile Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Carta Fundacional / Acta de Fundación) executed as a notarial public deed and subsequently registered at the Public Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum endowment of USD 10,000 (or assets of equivalent value) per Article 21 of Law 25 of 1995; the charter fixes the contribution schedule, and the law does not require an escrow bank deposit or full immediate disbursement; capital may subsist in cash, securities, or movable assets.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FOUNDATION COUNCIL RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF 2025. The Foundation Council of [FOUNDATION NAME] hereby resolves as follows: 1. The Foundation Charter, executed under Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995, is fully ratified and adopted. 2. The subscription of the initial endowment of USD 10,000 in lawful currency or equivalent assets is approved. 3. The registered office is established at the offices of the Resident Agent, [RESIDENT AGENT], whose appointment remains effective. 4. The following officers are appointed: Foundation Council President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each vested with representative powers. 5. The Resident Agent is authorized to file the Aviso de Operación, obtain the RUC tax identification, and open a corporate bank account for the Foundation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama — Corporate Names Department (Servicio de Búsqueda de Nombres)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal written name-search request, either personally at the Public Registry or through the authorized notary/law firm; verify that no identical or confusingly similar foundation or corporate name exists; the resulting certificate of name availability is valid for 30 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Completed name search application form
Photocopy of applicant or attorney passport/ID
Power of attorney executed before a notary (if filed by a representative)
Name search fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, immediately request a new search with an alternate name; no administrative appeal is necessary for alternative-name filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Circuit of Panama (Notaría del Circuito de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Charter in Spanish, setting forth the foundation name, purpose (ISIC 4791 online retail DTC brand), initial endowment, Council members, Protector (optional), Registered Office, Resident Agent, and asset disposition; the settlor appears before the notary, signs the deed, and the charter is incorporated into the notarial protocol; stamp taxes are collected at this stage.
required_dossiers: Notarized draft of the Foundation Charter in Spanish
Valid passport or ID of the settlor (Fundador)
Name availability certificate
Letter of acceptance from the Resident Agent (licensed Panamanian attorney)
Identification data and acceptance letters of Foundation Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects omissions, the deed may be re-drawn and re-executed by annexing corrective testimony; defective clauses are corrected before protocolization without registry penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Stamp Taxes and Registry Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá and the General Directorate of National Treasury (DGNT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, pay the foundational stamp tax and the Public Registry registration fee using the notarial protocol number; retain official receipts (cintillo de timbre and bank deposit slips) which must be attached to the registered deed copy.
required_dossiers: Notarial protocol reference number
Notary payment certificate (certificación del notario)
Official fee calculation sheet
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or treasury rejects payment due to incorrect fee calculation, request a recalculated treasury sheet from the notary and re-deposit within two business days; no substantive penalty applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation Charter at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama — Private Interest Foundations Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial protocol copy along with fee receipts to the Foundations Section; the registry performs legal examination (examen de legalidad) of the charter, verifies the Resident Agent, endowment clause, and object, then issues the Foundation Certificate of Registration; a certified copy of the registered deed is then released.
required_dossiers: Certified notarial protocol copy of the Foundation Charter
Original bank/treasury registry fee receipts
Petition sheet signed by the Resident Agent
Power of attorney of the Resident Agent (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an objection (reparo) or an improcedencia, the Resident Agent files a corrective sub-sanación or requests express review within 10 business days; alternatively, pay the expedited processing surcharge and obtain registration in 48 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Directorate of Revenues (Dirección General de Ingresos, DGI) — Ministry of Economy and Finance, with digital filing through the SUAE portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registry inscription, apply for the foundation's RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) using the certified deed and the Council appointment resolution; the DGI issues the RUC certificate; foundations without Panamanian-source income file a Nil Income Tax Declaration under the territorial tax regime.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Foundation Charter
Registered Foundation Council Resolution No. 1 (officer appointments)
Resident Agent identification and appointment letter
Certified copy of the foundation's registered address/official lease agreement
Valid identification of officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI flags discrepancies (e.g., address mismatch, missing certified copies), correct the document package and resubmit through the SUAE virtual window; the registry and DGI systems are synchronized, facilitating a 3-day cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Aviso de Operación (Business Operation Notice) for the Online Store
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama — Municipal Tax Authority through SUAE (Sistema Único de Avisos de Empresas), private entity and free-zone technical window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online Aviso de Operación on the SUAE/Invest in Panama platform using the RUC and the foundation's registered data; declare the activity as ISIC 4791 (internet retail of branded goods); the platform generates the municipal operating notice; no separate industrial license is required because the activity is an online DTC store without physical manufacturing or storefront.
required_dossiers: RUC registration certificate
Certified copy of the Foundation Charter and Council Resolution
Resident Agent acceptance letter
Description of the e-commerce platform (Shopify store URL) and payment rails (Shopify Payments, PayPal, Stripe)
Lease or address consent for the registered administrative office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality rejects the aviso due to zoning or activity classification, appeal to the Municipal Tax Authority with a revised ISIC description; for online-only businesses no public premise inspection is triggered, and approval is administrative.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 4791 DTC e-commerce; any ancillary warehousing would fall under the administrative control of the Municipality of Panama — Directorate of Municipal Revenue and Inspection, with no industrial license required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Business Operation Notice) issued by the Municipality of Panama via SUAE; no manufacturing or commercial operating permit is mandated for a pure online DTC brand store.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (Ministerio de Ambiente, MiAMBIENTE) — Directorate of Environmental Impact Assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I — Declaración de Impacto Ambiental (registration level) only if a physical office or storage facility is operated; pure online retail with no physical facility is exempt from a formal Environmental Impact Assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process discharges. Only domestic sanitary wastewater standards apply, per Ministry of Health regulations; no VOC or particulate emissions generated; electronic waste (e-waste) from returned/handled goods must be transferred to MiAMBIENTE-authorized collectors under General Environmental Law 41 of 1998.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: no public-assembly occupancy rating; registered administrative office must maintain basic fire extinguisher and evacuation compliance per the National Fire Department (Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá). Occupational clearance: MITRADEL (Ministry of Labor and Workforce Development) workplace health and safety standards under Executive Decree 30 of 2015; DTC remote operations with fewer than five on-site workers are exempt from the full Safety and Hygiene Committee (Comité de Seguridad e Higiene) requirement, but must comply with general employer obligations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) — the sole national tax administration; official electronic portal: E-Tax 2.0 (https://etax.mef.gob.pa) and DGI institutional site (https://www.dgi.gob.pa). The DGI administers the RUC registry, ISR (income tax), ITBMS (VAT), and e-invoicing clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the PIF under Law 25 of 1995 through a licensed Panamanian foundation agent and record the Pacto Fundacional and Reglamento with the Registro Público; the foundation agent acts as statutory resident agent and local tax representative. Step 2: After registry issuance, submit the RUC application (Formulario de Registro Único de Contribuyente) through E-Tax 2.0, attaching the certified foundation charter, the agent's appointment (Poder), the Council members' identification documents, and registered office proof; foreign officers may act by notarized/certified copies. Step 3: DGI validates and issues the RUC certificate (permanent TIN) within approximately 10–20 business days; if the PIF will conduct taxable operations in Panama, simultaneously register the ITBMS activity and, if annual revenue will not exceed PAB/USD 36,000, elect the small-taxpayer simplified regime in the same filing. Step 4: Obtain a digital signature certificate (Firma Electrónica) from the Autoridad de Innovación Gubernamental (AIG) to sign e-invoices and tax filings. Step 5: Register as an exporter in the SISCO/VUCEA customs single window (Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas and MICI) before exporting goods. A non-resident PIF without Panama-sourced activity still requires an RUC and must file annual sworn declarations claiming the territorial exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope. The PIF is a distinct legal person (hybrid foundation/corporation) taxed only on Panama-source income (Código Fiscal Article 693; Law 25 of 1995): (i) Panama-sourced business income is subject to corporate ISR at 25% of net taxable profits; (ii) foreign-source income, including export sales of goods and services rendered and consumed abroad, is outside Panama's income tax net; (iii) assets, capital contributions, and distributions to beneficiaries are exempt from gift/estate tax, and no wealth tax applies. A PIF conducting exclusively offshore DTC e-commerce (no sales to Panama customers, no employees or fixed place of business in Panama) operates as a de facto Tax_Exempt_Zone; however, Law 254 of 2021 economic substance rules require the PIF to either substantiate income as foreign-source or maintain adequate substance in Panama for any relevant activity performed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama domestic law does not provide US-style check-the-box or OECD hybrid-mismatch elections. Available statutory elections: (1) small-taxpayer regime election (Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente) for gross turnover ≤ PAB/USD 36,000, substituting full ITBMS accounting with a 2% simplified tax on sales; (2) multinational headquarters (SEM) election under Law 41 of 2007 for qualifying intra-group services, granting ITBMS/import-duty neutrality and preferential ISR treatment on qualifying net income; (3) economic substance report election under Law 254 of 2021 to classify the PIF as either a non-operating foreign-source vehicle or a Panama-resident entity performing relevant activities; (4) irrevocable vs. revocable foundation designation in the charter to define founder powers (does not alter Panamanian territorial tax classification but affects foreign CFC/attribution analysis). No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections are available under Panama domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) – national VAT, governed by Law 8 of 2010 as amended and the Código Fiscal.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Full ITBMS registration: no de minimis threshold – any person habitually transferring movable goods or providing taxable services in Panama must register before commencing operations. Simplified small-taxpayer regime: annual gross turnover ≤ PAB/USD 36,000, taxed at 2% of gross sales (replaces 7% ITBMS) with quarterly filing. Non-resident digital/e-commerce suppliers: Panama asserts ITBMS nexus for supplies electronically delivered to or consumed in Panama with no statutory turnover threshold; registration and a local fiscal representative are required for B2C digital sales, while physical export sales to non-residents fall outside the Panamanian taxable base.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) for all ITBMS-registered taxpayers, phased by DGI Resolution (large taxpayers from 2022; medium/small taxpayers from 2024). Issuance modes: (i) real-time online clearance through the DGI's SIFE platform (E-Tax 2.0) via web-service API, where each invoice XML is transmitted, validated, and stamped with the CSFE (Código de Seguridad de Facturación Electrónica); (ii) certified billing software (facturadores autorizados) integrating DGI's XSD schemas with OAuth-based authentication; (iii) e-ticket (tiquete) for point-of-sale retail. The PIF must configure its Shopify storefront/back-office to feed order data (customer, SKU, price, 0% export code) into the certified billing software, maintain sequential NOI (Número de Orden Interna) numbering, and reconcile each export parcel to a cleared e-invoice XML; failure to clear invoices in real time blocks issuance and attracts fines of PAB 300 to PAB 5,000 per invoice plus potential RUC suspension.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports qualify for 0% ITBMS under Law 8 of 2010. Cumulative criteria: (1) the PIF must be the seller of record (title and risk pass to the non-resident buyer per INCOTERM); (2) tangible goods must physically leave Panama within 30 days of invoicing, evidenced by customs dispatch; (3) the PIF must be registered as exporter in SISCO/VUCEA and the shipments declared through the customs export declaration process; (4) an e-invoice with zero-rated code ('exportación') must be cleared by DGI in real time; (5) services qualify only if rendered to a non-resident and consumed entirely abroad (no connection to Panamanian real estate or goods); (6) export proceeds must be credited to the PIF's Panamanian bank account. Shopify DTC sales to foreign consumers qualify if goods are posted/shipped from Panama to international addresses and the shipping documentation matches the e-invoice; sales delivered to Panamanian addresses are taxable at 7%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) processed through SISCO/VUCEA
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) proving physical exit from Panama
Commercial invoice (the DGI-cleared e-invoice XML bearing CSFE code)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank credit advice / Certificado de Abono) evidencing receipt of foreign proceeds
Proof of title transfer (order confirmation and INCOTERM terms)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas conduct matched audits of ITBMS returns, e-invoice XMLs, and SISCO export declarations. Recapture: if the zero-rating is not substantiated, the sale is reclassified as a domestic taxable transfer, and DGI assesses 7% ITBMS plus 1% monthly moratory interest, a 25% surcharge, and fines of 50%–100% of the omitted tax. Incorrect or fraudulent export declarations (overstated shipments, fictitious exporters, false bills of lading, unrepatriated proceeds) expose the PIF, its Council, and its registered agent to tax fraud and customs smuggling penalties under the Código Fiscal and Panama's Criminal Code, including imprisonment, confiscation of goods, cancellation of the exporter registration/RUC, and retrospective clawback of refunds claimed for up to six prior years. Records must be retained for at least seven years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama operates without a conventional central bank. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the statutory banking regulator and supervises all banking license categories under the Single Banking License regime (Legislative Decree 2 of 2008 and Law 52 of 2016). Banco Nacional de Panamá functions as the State's fiscal agent and operates the high-value USD clearing system (Sistema de Pagos de Alto Valor, SPAV). Monetary and exchange rate policy is de facto delegated to the U.S. Federal Reserve due to full dollarization; the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) administers external debt and fiscal policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy: the U.S. dollar is legal tender and the balboa circulates only as a token coin at par. There is no exchange control law, no capital account approval regime, and no restriction on conversion, repatriation, or cross-border transfer of funds in USD or any other currency. Current account and capital account transactions enjoy unlimited convertibility. Profit remittance for Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) is unrestricted at the FX level; however, territorial taxation imposes a 5% dividend withholding tax on distributions paid out of Panama-source profits attributable to shares registered with the Central Securities Depository, rising to 10% for unregistered/bearer-type distributions. Foreign-source income of the PIF, including revenues from a DTC e-commerce brand serving customers outside Panama, falls outside Panamanian tax jurisdiction if properly documented, making remittances tax-neutral at source under the territorial regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama does not impose any export proceeds surrender obligation, mandatory conversion ratio, repatriation timeline, or Central Bank approval for retention of export receipts. E-commerce and DTC brand sales proceeds from Shopify Payments, PayPal, Stripe, or direct-to-consumer card acquiring may be settled directly into a Panamanian corporate account in USD, EUR, GBP, or other settlement currency. Nevertheless, all international wire transactions involving the PIF must retain underlying commercial documentation for at least five (5) years to satisfy Article 19 of Law 23 of 2015 (Panama AML/CFT regime) and SBP Rule 006-2017 record keeping and transaction monitoring duties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low as a primary treasury rail. Offshore digital EMI institutions (Wise Platform, Revolut Business, Airwallex, and similar) are not licensed supervised banks by the SBP and cannot hold a Panamanian corporate account with full local clearing rights; they can serve only as downstream payout channels after principal funds are cleared through an SBP-supervised bank. Under the Panama Fintech Law (Law 121 of 2020) and the SBP Regulatory Sandbox, locally chartered fintech payment entities can provide IBAN-equivalent USD settlement, but none currently offers a fully production-grade integration with Shopify Payments or Stripe for the specific DTC use case. Legal constraints include: (i) EMIs must conduct UBO identification matching the PIF's Beneficial Ownership Registry data; (ii) source-of-funds documentation for all e-commerce sale settlements arriving from PSP aggregators is mandatory; and (iii) any EMI funneling funds to a PAN-licensed bank without clear purpose codes will trigger enhanced due diligence and possible account freezing under SBP Rule 006-2017.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person onboarding is effectively mandatory. Panamanian Tier-1 banks require each authorized signatory to attend a physical KYC interview at a branch in Panama before account activation. Fully remote opening for a Private Interest Foundation is not granted by any major bank; remote pre-approval is possible with apostilled foundation deed, registered regulations (Estatutos), council minutes appointing officers, UBO Registry certificate, and notarized powers of attorney, but biometric verification and wet-ink signature specimens must be completed in-country. An alternate compliant route is a professional Resident Agent or foundation service provider with a formal representation agreement and a limited power of attorney registered at the Public Registry; however, the primary beneficial owner or a senior Foundation Council member is still required to attend a document-signing ceremony at the bank's head office or an internationally recognized embassy-affiliated notary for complex structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficiary anonymity or reserved (undisclosed) beneficiary clauses in the PIF deed
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive UBO declaration submitted to the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (Executive Decree 363 of 2024); certified extract of the foundation deed disclosing beneficiary categories; Foundation Council resolution formally waiving beneficiary anonymity for banking purposes; source of wealth statement for all contributing founders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to evidence economic substance and territorial income application
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or service agreement proving physical management in Panama; council meeting minutes held at the registered Panamanian address; annual declaration on Form 730 confirming all e-commerce income is foreign-source; organization chart of the corporate service provider acting as Resident Agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency merchant settlements from PSP aggregators (Shopify Payments, Stripe, PayPal) bearing vague payment descriptions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform data extraction showing DTC store ownership and domain; Shopify store admin screenshots with product listings; monthly settlement reports from the PSPs; customer-side invoices and shipping documentation for sampled transactions; a written cash-flow narrative mapping PSP settlement to the PIF bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and politically exposed persons (PEP) screening hits on foreign e-commerce counterparties or supplier chains
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vendor resolution letters confirming no ownership by sanctioned parties; full customer and supplier identities; an external anti-bribery and OFAC sanctions screening report; refusal-to-deal policy for prescribed jurisdictions; contractual clauses restricting transaction with sanctioned countries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registration gap in the Beneficial Ownership Registry triggering bank de-risking
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official UBO registration certificate with the corresponding filing receipt of Panama's Tax Authority (DGI) using the system introduced in November 2024; sworn attorney statement confirming beneficial ownership details; payment receipt of the annual UBO fee; maintenance of a full or exempt status letter from DGI.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections must be executed through the SWIFT network using a correspondent relationship of the receiving Panamanian bank. Recommended practice is an MT103 wire from the founder's account to the PIF's operational USD account, using purpose code 'INTC' (intra-company) or 'EQUI' (equity-related payment) per ISO 20022 conventions. The PIF's foundation deed reference, the founder's name, and the UBO Registry identifier must appear in the beneficiary information field. If the injection is structured as a shareholder loan, execute a written loan agreement (secured or unsecured) with clear repayment schedule and use purpose code 'FCLT' (financial cash loan) to prevent FATCA and Anti-Money Laundering misclassification. For non-USD inflows (EUR, GBP), require the sending bank to convert to USD inside the correspondent bank; the Panamanian bank will record source-of-funds documentation for conversion. Verify that the receiving bank's compliance office receives the payment instruction and the underlying foundation documentation at least 48 hours before funds value date to avoid suspension of the credit under SBP Rule 006-2017 'no-pass-through' expectations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements are selected based on counterparty preference and invoice currency. For general supplier payments, use SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'GDDS' (goods trade) or 'TRAD' (trade payment), maintaining a commercial invoice and bill of lading or fulfilment receipt in the treasury archive. For larger DTC inventory purchases exceeding USD 250,000, a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) issued by the Panamanian bank through a confirmed correspondent bank is advisable to mitigate goods risk; terms are typically 30-90 day usance with documents against payment. Local USD-denominated trades and partner payouts inside Panama may clear through the ACH system operated by the Panamanian Chamber of Commerce (ACH Panamá) or high-value through SPAV via Banco Nacional. For e-commerce refunds to consumers, the most efficient rails are the PSP's built-in refund API (Shopify Payments/Stripe/PayPal) which re-route funds from the PIF's merchant balance, avoiding costly MT103 reversals. FX conversion for outbound EUR/GBP payables is executed at the bank's spot desk with a same-day or next-day value; all FX trades must reference the underlying invoice and obtain a transaction number from the bank's trading floor for audit traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot for USD/EUR, USD/GBP, USD/MXN and other convert pairs offered by the Panamanian commercial banking center; the USD is domestic legal tender so the PIF's balance sheet is naturally hedged against local currency fluctuations

Deliverable foreign exchange forwards (outrights) up to 12 months under the international banking center's standard ISDA or amortizing master agreements; typical counterparties are Banco General, Banistmo, or Scotiabank Panama
Cross-currency interest rate swaps negotiated via international bank branches in Panama for matched asset-liability hedging of EUR or GBP revenue streams

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging market currencies (MXN, BRL, COP, TRY) booked through subsidiary treasury desks of foreign banks located in the Panama International Banking Center, subject to external ISDA documentation and Collateral Support Annex

Vanilla FX options (European style) for protection against unexpected appreciation of GBP or EUR against the USD, only where the bank has a local derivatives license and the PIF maintains adequate collateral arrangements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Government Fee (Tasa Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 March (first quarter window)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: USD 50 per full month of late payment; after 3 consecutive unpaid years, the Registro Público may annotate the foundation's file and initiate administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Anual de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March of the following fiscal year (calendar-year basis); required for any RUC-registered foundation even with zero taxable income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines from USD 20 up to USD 5,000, monthly 1% late-payment interest on confirmed tax dues, and issuance of negative 'persona jurídica al día' certificates blocking bank and notarial transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements / Accounting Disclosures (when Panamanian-source gross revenue exceeds threshold)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual income tax return; mandatory presentation if Panamanian-source gross revenue exceeds USD 50,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Tax Code Article 706 non-presentation surcharges; fines up to USD 5,000; financial statements must be prepared under IFRS or recognized Local GAAP.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Formulario 930 – Transactions with Third/Related Parties (threshold-based information return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April for the preceding calendar year; applicable only to DGI-registered foundations exceeding statutory transaction thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary fines under the Panamanian Tax Code for failure to file information returns, plus monthly surcharges on any underlying omitted tax liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory external audit for a Private Interest Foundation engaged in passive/holding activity; a Panama-CPA financial-statement report is mandatory when Panamanian-source gross income exceeds USD 50,000, and a full audited opinion by a licensed Panama CPA is required when such income exceeds USD 3,000,000.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (IASB) as adopted in Panama for tax-reporting entities; IFRS for SMEs permitted below specified thresholds; foundation internal books under Law 25 of 1995 Art. 21 may be kept in English or Spanish and in USD/B/., using IFRS or a consistently applied cash-basis internal framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 254 of 2020 and the Panamanian Beneficial Ownership Registry (RTBF), the foundation must file the final beneficial owner declaration at incorporation; declarations cannot be amended or certificates obtained if the filing is incomplete. Any actual change in economic beneficiaries must be declared within 30 days, with no separate statutory annual re-filing; best-practice annual confirmation by the resident agent is recommended to maintain the RTBF certification valid for banking, DGI, and payment-processor due diligence.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Foundation Council and Protector Resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – 8,000 (only if DGI threshold or processor/bank governance requires a signed audit opinion)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard CIT under Código Fiscal Art. 713; applied only to Panamanian-source taxable income under the territorial regime)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Private Interest Foundations under Law 25 of 1995 are structurally exempt from Panamanian income tax, stamp tax, municipal taxes, and transfer taxes on foundation assets to the extent the foundation does not engage in commercial activity in Panama and derives income from assets or activities abroad. A PIF operating an offshore DTC Shopify webstore therefore bears 0% Panamanian CIT on non-Panama revenue. ITBMS (VAT at 7%) is chargeable only on taxable supplies consumed in Panama.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 745 - Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta para Personas Jurídicas, filed electronically through the DGI e-filing portal (DGI en Línea / e-Tax) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF). A PIF without Panamanian-source income has no Form 745 exposure; compliance is limited to the annual Public Registry foundation fee (USD 150) and, where required, the Beneficial Ownership filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual CIT declaration; quarterly advance payments (pagos fraccionados) apply only to CIT taxpayers with prior-year liability (instalments due 31 March / 30 June / 30 September / 31 December). Exempt PIFs stand outside the advance-payment regime.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form 745 must be filed within three months of the fiscal year-end; for the standard 1 January - 31 December fiscal year the deadline is 31 March of the following year. Non-filing taxpayers become subject to DGI estimated assessments on the 'base cierta' basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer's unique RUC number, foundation folio at the Registro Público, and legal name of the PIF.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIF is entered by the registered agent using the foundation folio and the agent's Panamanian address and email as mandatory contact data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting period with start and end dates (e.g., 01-Jan-2024 to 31-Dec-2024).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A newly formed PIF may use a short first period ending 31 December; no annualization adjustments apply to PIFs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Self-classification as general territorial CIT regime or exempt passive foundation under Law 25 of 1995.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark 'foreign-source only / exempt foundation' and attach a council-certified statement confirming no Panamanian commercial activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4a - Gross Income from Panamanian Sources
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenue derived from sales, services, or assets located or exploited in Panama (e.g., DTC shipments to Panama-resident customers and local fulfillment services).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only the portion of Shopify settlement proceeds attributable to customers physically resident in Panama; all foreign customer revenue is excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from activities or asset use outside Panama; non-taxable under the territorial system.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Shopify, PayPal, and Stripe settlement reports evidencing customer country of delivery and payment provenance; retain the evidence in the DTC data room.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs and deductions allocated only against Panamanian-source taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt non-residents leave cost base unallocated; foreign marketing and platform fees must not be deducted against Panama-source revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 - Net Taxable Base and Tax at 25%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after territorial deductions, multiplied by 25% to arrive at annual CIT payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt PIF enters zero; if Panamanian activity is accidentally triggered, tax is computed solely on the Panama-source portion of revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 8 - Withholdings, Advances and Dividend Tax Report
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for pagos fraccionados and Panamanian withholdings; reporting of the 10% withholding tax on dividends paid out of Panama-taxed profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PIF distributions to beneficiaries are not corporate dividends and are not subject to Panamanian withholding; leave nil and sign under oath.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 745: DGI imposes a monthly late-payment surcharge of 5% of the unpaid tax (maximum 100%) plus moratory interest, an administrative fine of USD 50 to USD 500 per infraction, daily surcharges for continued non-compliance, suspension of the 'paz y salvo' tax certificate, and estimated assessment where the DGI reconstructs income. Willful omission of Panama-source revenue triggers criminal tax-fraud sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid by a Panama corporation out of Panamanian-taxed profits (withholding at source by the payer); 0% on dividends declared out of foreign-source profits and on PIF distributions to beneficiaries under Law 25 of 1995, because foundation distributions are not dividends of a commercial company.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's DTA network is limited but operative (e.g., South Korea, Mexico, Barbados, Qatar-type treaties). The process to invoke treaty relief is: (i) obtain a Certificado de Residencia Fiscal (TRC) from the DGI, which requires that the PIF be tax-resident and economically managed in Panama; (ii) deliver the TRC and a beneficial-ownership declaration to the Panamanian dividend payer before distribution; (iii) apply the reduced treaty rate at source, or file a refund claim with the DGI within the statutory claim period if the domestic 10% withholding was deducted; and (iv) comply with MLI principal-purpose-test and transparency conditions where applicable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: Panama does not impose withholding tax on outbound interest paid to non-residents where the capital is deployed offshore or the lender is abroad, in line with the territorial regime. Royalties: no Panamanian WHT applies to IP exploited outside Panama; where a trademark or brand is exploited in the Panamanian market, the royalty is Panamanian-source income and the payer must satisfy DGI collection through withholding at the statutory rate or self-assessment, with treaty rates available under the relevant DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 2,000,000 (Panama is a dollarized economy; PAB/USD is 1:1) in aggregate related-party transactions in a fiscal year triggers the mandatory Local File and the annual Form 780 transfer-pricing declaration; Master File documentation is required where intercompany transactions exceed USD 8,000,000; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of USD 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not impose a separate BVI/CAY-style Economic Substance Regulation filing on PIFs; however, substance is decisive in four areas: (i) territorial sourcing — income is Panamanian-source where the foundation council manages and executes the DTC business from Panama; (ii) TRC issuance — substantive presence (local office, staff, real decision-making) is required to obtain treaty relief; (iii) AML/UBO — Law 196 of 2019 obliges the Resident Agent to file beneficial ownership with the Registro Público and to evidence genuine economic substance of the PIF; and (iv) anti-shamming — banks and payment processors will freeze settlement rails if the PIF cannot demonstrate premises, personnel, and real transactions. A PIF that merely interposes a Panama wrapper around a Shopify store while all business is run outside Panama preserves its territorial exemption, but the moment Panamanian management or local customers appear, the DGI will re-source the profit and tax it retroactively.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - False Foreign-Source Allocation of DTC Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The PIF books 100% of Shopify, PayPal, and Stripe settlements as 'foreign-source' on its books and Form 745 while logistics, pricing decisions, trademarks, and a Panama fulfillment address serve customers physically located in Panama; no ITBMS (7%) is charged on Panama deliveries and no territorial apportionment is made.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI reassessment at 25% CIT on the entire mis-sourced Panama revenue plus ITBMS, monthly late-payment surcharges (5% per month, cap 100%), moratory interest, and understatement penalties; criminal prosecution for defraudación fiscal under Panamanian law carries imprisonment of 2-5 years and fines, in addition to blacklisting and cancellation of the trading license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The foundation council members, the settlor as economic owner, and the signing registered agent are jointly and severally liable for the recaptured taxes; the DGI may pierce the foundation's autonomous patrimony on proof of simulation; criminal sentencing includes restitution of evaded taxes, management bans, and travel restrictions.
